notes: Independent one-page ink reading. Whole and each half were viewed once. Twelve genuinely open local places were cropped once each, enlarged to 2800 pixels across with Pillow LANCZOS and autocontrast; no sharpening was applied. Upper and lower margin notes were rotated as logged. Every crop was viewed once; no image display failed.

The page is a typescript with handwritten mathematical signs, marginal comments, insertion guides, cancellations and margin rules. Handwritten additions are attributed only to an unnamed hand; no personal identity or material is inferred. Heading underline makers are not securely assigned.

Title: Théorème de Bertini et variantes. The page contains theorem 1, local statement 2, corollary 3, a remark with a superposed 4/3 number, and the opening of corollary 4 (de 1). It has three displayed fundamental-group maps, no commutative diagram, no substantive drawing beyond margin marks, no date, no stated total-page count and no own page number. The pencil 112 is an archive number.

The document claims geometric irreducibility of a generic linear section under a dimension bound; a local unibranch/normal/smooth variant; and surjectivity of the indicated fundamental-group maps with the qualifications written in the remark. The final corollary begins and is incomplete on this scan. These are reported claims, not checked theorems.

Written reservation transcribed exactly: “On n’affirme pas, cependant, que (*) soit toujours surjectif (sans hypothèse de propreté sur X).” This concerns unrestricted surjectivity; nothing here has been construed as an admission that the preceding proper-case statement lacks a proof.

The mathematical setting made the X/Y source in (**) and the prime-to-characteristic wording worth inspecting. Neither the preceding map nor the expected word exposant was used to settle the ink. Both mixed cells retain alternatives; the source’s overprint order is unknown.

The consecutive statement numbers were not used to choose the remark numeral. Its 4/3 contours are retained without asserting deleted/replacement order. Likewise no chronological deletion is assigned to d/x overprinting.

Enoncé without an initial accent, non respé., and the slash in déduit/formellement are preserved. The nearly upright accent in è...posant is newly left open between grave and acute, rather than silently normalised to e.

H’s section heading and bold/emphasis wrappers are treated as editorial typography where they encode the same textual heading or emphasis. Absence of handwritten wrappers alone is not a difference. Actual additions, cancellations, note omissions and locations are recorded separately. The two display labels are physically on the left; reading.tex explicitly places its tag content there.

Input limitation: the C_prior_questions.md version initially supplied included two unrelated scan-116 excerpts. They were ignored; no scan-116 source or other page was opened. The parent later confirmed removal of those administrative remnants; this did not change any image reading. The notation snapshot was read only as provisional notation guidance, never as authority for this page.

No OCR, recognition package, internet search, external mathematical text, other reader’s output, extra agent, or other page image was used. No proof verification, computation, or formal certificate was performed; checks is therefore empty.

Local-heading layout refinement from the already viewed c03 crop: the only independent low underline belongs to the cancelled Complément line and stops before the end of the raised Enoncé local. The raised heading is therefore not separately underlined in reading.tex. This is a stroke-location decision, not an inference about intended emphasis.

Output structure was checked locally: required report fields and allowed difference kinds are present, all 12 crop paths exist, and reading.tex has balanced braces, display delimiters and TikZ environment delimiters. These are file checks, not mathematical checks.
